target_customer: Managers and small teams who build and present project schedules and were using Microsoft Project
problem: Managers spent hours rebuilding project schedules and slide decks from the same data; Gantto made a free web based Gantt chart tool where schedules could be built, shared and presented from the app.
business_model: Web SaaS, free at launch with paid plans later (per TechCrunch launch coverage; pricing details not captured)
product_category: Web based project scheduling and Gantt charts

founders.name: Christopher R. Carlson
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch launch post says the founders previously worked at an unnamed medical robotics company where they rebuilt Microsoft Project charts by hand in PowerPoint.

founders.name: Federico Barbagli
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; no biography given.

exit.reason: Tom's Planner said it bought Gantto for its market position and active user base and would phase out the Gantto product because of a different technology stack.

competitors.name: Microsoft Project
competitors.what: Desktop standard for project scheduling and Gantt charts, the explicit target of Gantto
competitors.traction_then: Reported to have more than 20 million users

competitors.name: Basecamp
competitors.what: Web based project management product named as a web competitor

technical_complexity.rationale: An interactive browser Gantt chart editor with task dependencies and in app presenting was nontrivial in 2010 browsers, but it was ordinary web engineering for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Project files create some lock in, but several web Gantt tools launched around the same time and Tom's Planner already served a larger user base; the acquirer said Gantto had a different stack and would be retired.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought it. A direct competitor, Tom's Planner, acquired Gantto on 8 July 2013 and planned to phase the product out.

market_need_then: Microsoft Project had more than 20 million users, and the founders felt the pain themselves of rebuilding schedules by hand as slides each week; TechCrunch cited the large installed base as evidence of potential in 2010.

branding.name_origin: A play on words on Gantt chart, per the company description on the YC page; Henry Gantt popularized the chart.
branding.domain_note: gantto.com later redirected to Tom's Planner after the 2013 acquisition (observed on fetch).

identity.voice_and_tone: YC tagline was Better Microsoft Project

brand_strength.rationale: A clear pun and plain tagline made the product easy to understand, and press coverage existed at launch, but no sources show community, merch or brand driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Gantto launched publicly on 13 August 2010 as a web based alternative to Microsoft Project and reached roughly 40,000 users by 2013 according to TechCrunch, about a third of Tom's Planner's base. It raised almost nothing publicly and was bought by its competitor Tom's Planner in July 2013 for undisclosed terms, which planned to retire the product, so it ended as a small product exit rather than a venture outcome.
notes: The YC directory marks Gantto Inactive while sources show an acquisition by Tom's Planner. CB Insights (single database) reports $20K over 2 rounds with a seed dated 2010-06-26 and lists Tom's Planner as an investor; the second round and amounts are not verified, and a search summary mentioned 500 Startups as a backer that I could not confirm. The Xconomy 2012 article returned 503 and was not read. The TechCrunch acquisition post, as summarized, called Tom Ummels Gantto's CEO, which looks like a mix up with the Tom's Planner founder; I did not record him as a Gantto founder. The Tom's Planner post said users included Twitter and Lucasfilm. No dedicated company website remained (gantto.com redirects to Tom's Planner); the YC page lists no website.
